text:
**Spending abroad:** No. You can pay anywhere in any currency with your Monzo card, fee-free. Monzo passes Mastercard's exchange rate on to you with no extra charges.

**Cash withdrawals:** These are free up to a limit, and the limit depends on your account. If Monzo is your main bank account, withdrawals are unlimited and fee-free in the EEA. Anywhere else you get £200 every 30 days, then a 3% fee.

Monzo's help page gives this breakdown for UK customers (it's an older page, so check the app for current figures):

| Account | UK & EEA | Outside EEA |
|---|---|---|
| Monzo isn't your main bank | £400 fee-free per 30 days, then 3% | £200 fee-free per 30 days, then 3% |
| Monzo is your main bank | Unlimited fee-free | £200 fee-free per 30 days, then 3% |
| Monzo Plus | Unlimited fee-free | £400 fee-free per 30 days, then 3% |
| Premium, Perks & Max | Unlimited fee-free | £600 fee-free per 30 days, then 3% |

Source: Monzo Help

- **ATM operators:** Some ATMs charge their own fee, which Monzo doesn't receive. Use a free machine when you can.
- **Local currency:** If you use an ATM abroad, it can be worth withdrawing in the local currency to avoid additional conversion fees. If the ATM offers to charge you in pounds, decline.
- **"Main bank" status:** Monzo defines this as having your salary paid into Monzo.

One result claimed a flat £2 fee per withdrawal. That doesn't match Monzo's own pages, so I wouldn't rely on it. Monzo's Irish pages show different euro-based rules, but those apply to Irish accounts, not yours.

Your exact allowance is shown in the Monzo app, so check it before you travel.
